back: The brain (the model and its loop), the hands (the sandboxes and tools), and the event log (the record of the run, which only grows at the end).
front: What are the three parts of a managed agent?

back: It records each turn, call and result as it happens, so a new process can read what already ran.
front: What is an event log for?

back: Each part can fail and be replaced alone. A new sandbox can take over the hands while the log and the brain keep going.
front: Why does the split help when a part fails?

back: With the brain, outside the sandbox. The hands run code the model wrote, so a key inside them can be read.
When you would rather not run the brain, the hands and the log yourself, and the service's terms fit your data.
front: When does a managed service fit better than your own harness?

back: False, when the log lives outside the process. Without the log, the run starts over and repeats its side effects.
